primary_sources: GitHub Pages Developer Portfolio Best Practices

rules.explanation: Visitors and recruiters decide whether to stay on a portfolio within the first 5 seconds. The Hero Section must clearly state your engineering discipline, core stack, and target role.
rules.do: Include a clear headline, concise intro statement (e.g., 'Embedded Systems & AI Engineer'), and primary Call-To-Action (Resume Download / Contact).
rules.dont: Do not leave the top banner ambiguous with vague inspirational quotes or missing technical titles.

rules.explanation: Portfolios should prioritize quality over quantity. Displaying 3-5 high-impact, fully documented projects is more effective than listing dozens of incomplete tutorials.
rules.do: Feature top 3-5 flagship projects with architecture diagrams, live demo links, source code, and key metrics.
rules.dont: Do not flood the showcase with basic course assignments or incomplete repositories without documentation.

rules.explanation: A slow or non-responsive portfolio creates a negative impression of your technical execution. Pages should load under 2 seconds and render cleanly on mobile.
rules.do: Ensure 100% mobile responsiveness, optimize image sizes, and maintain high performance (Lighthouse score > 90).
rules.dont: Do not use uncompressed heavy assets or broken layout grids on smaller screen sizes.

rules.rule_name: Direct Access to Resume and Contact Channels
rules.explanation: Recruiters should never have to search for how to reach you or download your paper CV.
rules.do: Provide a prominent 'Download Resume' button (PDF) and active links to LinkedIn, GitHub, and professional Email in the header/footer.
rules.dont: Do not hide contact info behind complex contact forms without direct email fallback.
